title: Business software study: project tool pricing pages
persona: Taylor leads a 5-person analytics team in New York and is choosing a project management tool. Budget: about $15 per user per month (about $75 per month for the team), ideally billed monthly. Must-haves: dashboards for project status, a Google Sheets or Excel integration, and free guest access for 2 client contacts. Taylor dislikes annual-only pricing, features hidden behind 'contact sales', and unclear trial or cancellation terms. Do not invent prices, limits, or terms. Taylor will not sign up, start a trial, log in, or give any contact details during this study.
model_validation: candidate; requires paid pilot and human review

tasks.goal: Find the plan on this site that best fits your team size, must-haves, and budget. Read the plan name and its displayed per-user price, and note whether that price is billed monthly or annually. Do not sign up, start a trial, or contact sales.

For the selected plan, check the limits that matter to you (seats, dashboards, integrations, guest access, storage) and the monthly versus annual price for 5 users. State what is missing or only available on a higher plan rather than guessing.

Find the free trial length, whether a credit card is needed, and the cancellation or refund terms, using only public pages. Explain whether you would continue with this tool or leave, and what remains unknown. This is a synthetic preference, not a real purchase.
